kpk2tdsPh0A.summary: Pannenkoek2012's commentated tool-assisted Super Mario 64 run collecting the Watch for Rolling Rocks star with half an A press, using parallel universes and QPU movement. The video is marked outdated in favor of a newer version.
kpk2tdsPh0A.why: Held up as a legendary deep dive into game internals, explained lucidly and with humor, and a gateway to the channel.

kBdfcR-8hEY.summary: The first episode of Michael Sandel's Harvard course on moral reasoning, opening with the trolley problem and the choice between killing one to save five. Sandel draws out student arguments and introduces utilitarian and other approaches to justice.
kBdfcR-8hEY.why: One of the most frequently recommended online lecture series on HN, praised for giving people vocabulary to examine ethical positions and for Sandel's skilled teaching.

k2h2lvhzMDc.summary: Ed Catmull of Pixar speaks at Stanford's 2007 Entrepreneurship Conference on running a creative company. He argues for surfacing small problems early and building good teams, with stories like the Toy Story 2 crunch.
k2h2lvhzMDc.why: Repeatedly called one of the most useful talks on building organizations and managing creative teams.

kZRE7HIO3vk.summary: Casey Muratori's long talk arguing that modern software has ballooned to tens of millions of lines because of hardware and OS diversity. He proposes a stable ISA for entire system-on-a-chip packages and recalls when games shipped with their own boot disk.
kZRE7HIO3vk.why: HN recommends it, long as it is, as an eye-opening rant on software complexity and why systems became so complicated.

kCc8FmEb1nY.summary: Andrej Karpathy builds a GPT from scratch in code, following Attention Is All You Need and GPT-2/3, in about two hours using PyTorch. He connects it to ChatGPT and assumes familiarity with his earlier makemore videos.
kCc8FmEb1nY.why: It is the go-to recommendation for learning how transformers and LLMs actually work, praised for its clarity and Karpathy's teaching.

kF9KretXqJw.summary: A 2018 lecture, with subtitles available, by former Finnish intelligence colonel Martti J. Kari on Russian strategic culture. He walks through the historical layers of Russia and explains why the country behaves as it does.
kF9KretXqJw.why: After the 2022 invasion, commenters spread it widely as an eye-opening explanation of Russian mindset, corruption and propaganda, though a few doubt the presenter's rigor.

kjBOesZCoqc.summary: A five-minute preview of 3Blue1Brown's Essence of Linear Algebra series, which uses animation to build geometric intuition for topics from a standard linear algebra course.
kjBOesZCoqc.why: HN repeatedly recommends the series as the best intuition-first, visual introduction to linear algebra and a benchmark for clear math explanation.

kYHTzqHIngk.summary: A four-minute Not Just Bikes comparison of grocery shopping in Amsterdam versus car-centric North America, arguing that frequent small fresh-food trips beat bulk shopping. It ties this to land use and reduced food waste.
kYHTzqHIngk.why: Linked in urbanism and car-dependence threads as a concise case for walkable fresh-food shopping.

kYfNvmF0Bqw.summary: A short excerpt from a 1994 interview of Steve Jobs in which he says everything around us was made up by people no smarter than you, and that you can change and shape the world.
kYfNvmF0Bqw.why: Quoted in threads on motivation, agency and regret as an encouraging reminder that the world can be changed.

kTiP0zKF9bc.summary: Valve's John McDonald presents at GDC 2018 on how Valve uses deep learning (VACnet) to detect cheaters in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive. He covers training on human-reviewed replays and how model output is confirmed by manual review.
kTiP0zKF9bc.why: The go-to link in any anti-cheat thread for a concrete, well-delivered account of machine-learning cheat detection in production.

kc9HwsxE1OY.summary: Julia co-creator Stefan Karpinski explains why multiple dispatch makes Julia code and types reusable across packages with so little friction. He covers sharing basic types and sharing generic algorithms.
kc9HwsxE1OY.why: HN commenters recommend it as the definitive explanation, from a language designer, of why multiple dispatch makes Julia's composability work.

k1kndKWJKB8.summary: The first part of Extra History's animated miniseries on the South Sea Bubble. It explains how England's government debt led Robert Harley to turn to financier John Blunt, whose schemes began inflating artificial demand for shares.
k1kndKWJKB8.why: Recommended as an accessible, easily digestible introduction to the South Sea Bubble whenever financial manias, ICOs or overvalued companies come up.

kya_LXa_y1E.summary: Physicist Angela Collier's roughly hour-long video on how string theory was hyped to the public and what that did to science communication. She traces the history of the theory as a narrative and argues it is interesting but was oversold.
kya_LXa_y1E.why: Recommended as an engaging critique of string theory hype and its effect on public trust in physics, and often cited alongside Peter Woit's writing.

kU3BceoMuaA.summary: Techmoan's 45-minute retrospective on Sony's MiniDisc, covering the first and last machines, ATRAC, MD-LP, Net-MD and HiMD. It argues the format deserves more credit than its US failure narrative suggests.
kU3BceoMuaA.why: The standard recommendation for MiniDisc history, especially as a non-American counterpoint to the failed-format story.

kUfF2MTnqAw.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day undergoes hypoxia training and experiences his own impaired thinking as oxygen is withdrawn. The video shows how quickly and unnoticeably oxygen deprivation degrades judgment, illustrating why you put your own mask on first.
kUfF2MTnqAw.why: It is the go-to demonstration of how hypoxia silently disables decision making, cited in threads on altitude, flying, diving, CO2 and breathwork.

kZA9Hnp3aV4.summary: A recording of physicist Albert Bartlett's well-known lecture on the arithmetic of exponential growth, applied to population and energy use. He argues that steady percentage growth in a finite world cannot continue and sneaks up suddenly.
kZA9Hnp3aV4.why: Treated as the classic lecture on why people misjudge exponential growth, and pulled out in threads on compound growth, epidemics, crypto and resource limits.

k7X7sZzSXYs.summary: An animated short film of Tanya Davis's spoken-word poem 'How To Be Alone', illustrated by Andrea Dorfman. It gently argues that being alone can be embraced and enjoyed.
k7X7sZzSXYs.why: HN commenters point lonely people to it as a moving, comforting piece of art about getting comfortable with solitude.

klaJqofCsu4.summary: Big Clive tears down the Dubai lamp, a Philips LED bulb developed with Dubai's ruler for maximum efficiency and long life. He examines its construction and circuitry, including underrun LEDs and many filament strips.
klaJqofCsu4.why: HN points to it as proof that efficient, long-lived LED bulbs can be built and as an example of well-designed lamps.

krfcq5pF8u8.summary: Ava DuVernay's Oscar-nominated documentary on how the history of racial inequality in the US, from slavery through the 13th Amendment's exception clause, drives mass incarceration. It combines archival footage with testimony from activists and scholars.
krfcq5pF8u8.why: HN commenters strongly recommend it as a clear examination of structural racism in the criminal justice system and the war on drugs, and note it is free to watch.

kH5APw_SLUU.summary: A University of Michigan Medicine demonstration of building a cheap DIY air purifier from a box fan and a HEPA or high-MERV filter using hardware-store parts. It explains why this helps against dust, smoke and viruses and ties it to local air quality readings.
kH5APw_SLUU.why: HN people link it during wildfire smoke and air quality threads as a practical, cheap fix, though a few doubt how rigorously its effectiveness was shown.

kd2KEHvK-q8.summary: LEMMiNO's 25-minute documentary on the 2014 disappearance of Malaysia Airlines Flight 370. It walks through the official investigation's findings and the leading theories, including satellite data and hydrophone recordings.
kd2KEHvK-q8.why: Regularly shared as the best well-made overview of the MH370 mystery, in threads on the search and ocean mapping.

kfg_e6YG37U.summary: Kelly Starrett's Talks at Google presentation on staying healthy while desk bound, mixing anatomy and practical mobility advice. It shows how to set up a desk and sit and move to avoid pain.
kfg_e6YG37U.why: Often the first thing suggested to HN programmers asking about posture and back pain.

kh88fVP2FWQ.summary: CGP Grey explains why "Indian" is often preferred over "Native American" in the United States, especially near reservations, and how many tribes exist in the US. He draws on conversations with people who identify as Indian.
kh88fVP2FWQ.why: Cited again and again in terminology debates as a convincing source that many American Indians prefer the term Indian.

klTjiXjqHrQ.summary: Bret Victor's talk proposing a new kind of maker space built for seeing and understanding a project's behavior: inside it, across time and across possibilities. It argues for scientific understanding over recipes and rules of thumb.
klTjiXjqHrQ.why: Listed alongside his other talks as foundational context for Dynamicland and visual-programming ideas, and he is the most frequently cited speaker on such threads.

kmFOBoy2MZ8.summary: Isaac Arthur's in-depth look at what it would take to settle and eventually terraform Mars. He covers the challenges and the scale of the work needed to make it a home for humanity.
kmFOBoy2MZ8.why: Recommended as a thorough, speculative-but-grounded overview of the magnitude of colonizing Mars.

krB0enBeSiE.summary: A roughly three-hour Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Brendan Eich, creator of JavaScript and co-founder of Mozilla and Brave. It covers JavaScript's rushed creation at Netscape, the browser wars, Firefox and Mozilla, and Brave's privacy approach.
krB0enBeSiE.why: Linked as a source for first-hand JavaScript and Netscape history, with commenters pointing to specific segments like the Java versus JavaScript decision.

k1BneeJTDcU.summary: Bo Burnham's song from his special Inside, a satirical take on internet culture, attention and extremism.
k1BneeJTDcU.why: HN commenters bring it up in threads about the internet, attention economy and smartphones, mostly as a favorite, with a few dissenters.

k6U-i4gXkLM.summary: First lecture of MIT 6.00, an introductory computer science course taught in Python by Eric Grimson and John Guttag. It covers the goals of the course, what computation is, and data types, operators and variables.
k6U-i4gXkLM.why: HN commenters recommend it as a simple, direct entry point for beginners who want to learn computer science, not just programming.

kPR8h4-qZdk.summary: Nicholas Ormrod's CppCon 2016 talk on how Facebook optimizes std::string with its open-source replacement fbstring. It covers storage layout tradeoffs, small string optimization and memory allocation behavior.
kPR8h4-qZdk.why: HN returns to it as the go-to talk on string internals, small string packing and why small percentage optimizations matter at scale.

kPRA0W1kECg.summary: A visualization and sonification of 15 sorting algorithms, from selection sort to bogo sort, run on shuffled integers in six minutes. Each algorithm gets a size and speed scaled to its complexity.
kPRA0W1kECg.why: A classic that HN points to for seeing how sorting algorithms behave, valued for how satisfying it is to watch and hear.

knUitQQnpJo.summary: A three-hour PyCon 2016 tutorial by Christophe Pettus that orients Python developers to PostgreSQL. It covers installation, administration, and use, including vacuuming, MVCC, replication and backups.
knUitQQnpJo.why: HN readers recommend it as a thorough, practical introduction to Postgres fundamentals and optimization for application developers.

kYYJlNbV1OM.summary: The opening lecture of Jordan Peterson's 2017 University of Toronto personality course. He defines personality from historical, constructivist, psychoanalytic, behavioral and neuropsychological angles.
kYYJlNbV1OM.why: Recommended as part of a long lecture series on psychology, complementing biology lectures, and named when HN asks for the best lecture series.

k_5M-z_RUKA.summary: A one-hour documentary on XBAND, the 1994 modem network for the Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis. It covers matchmaking, chat, email, leaderboards and how games were patched at runtime to cope with lag.
k_5M-z_RUKA.why: HN recommends it as a fascinating engineering story of early console online play, including a working demo.

k1luKAS_Xcg.summary: Esther Gokhale's short TEDx talk argues that the natural human spine is curved rather than straight and teaches a 'primal posture' for sitting without back pain.
k1luKAS_Xcg.why: Recommended in back pain and posture threads as a short, practical idea that helped some commenters.

kb-m2fasdDY.summary: Matt Ranney of Uber talks at GOTO Chicago 2016 about what Uber learned from growing past 1,000 production microservices. He covers regrets, sprawl and organizational effects.
kb-m2fasdDY.why: Often brought up as an honest account of microservice sprawl, including the fact that nobody at Uber knew exactly how many services existed.

kfM-yu0iQBk.summary: The first part of Freya Holmer's three-part, nearly four-hour lecture on shader coding for game devs in Unity. It covers what shaders are, vertex and fragment shaders, interpolators, data types, blending and textures.
kfM-yu0iQBk.why: Recommended as a good first-steps shader tutorial that also teaches broad graphics knowledge.

kixAljyfdqU.summary: PBS Space Time explains the Higgs field and how the Higgs mechanism gives particles mass within quantum field theory. It is a ten-minute overview for a lay audience.
kixAljyfdqU.why: Recommended as a clear explanation of how electrons gain mass, and the channel itself gets binge-watch praise.

klpDHn8viX8.summary: A PBS Space Time episode explaining the holographic principle: the idea that our 3+1 dimensional universe may be described by information on a lower-dimensional boundary. It walks through black hole entropy and the AdS/CFT correspondence.
klpDHn8viX8.why: HN commenters point to it as an accessible way to get a grip on AdS/CFT and the holographic principle whenever black holes or information physics come up.

kgCUn4fQTsc.summary: Bloomberg Technology interviews Google engineer Blake Lemoine about the experiments that led him to believe LaMDA was sentient and why he was placed on administrative leave. He also raises concerns about AI ethics at Google.
kgCUn4fQTsc.why: HN commenters recommend watching it to hear his side directly, noting he comes across as coherent, while others dispute his sincerity.

kBLkX2VaQs4.summary: A short clip of Louis CK on Conan riffing that everything is amazing and nobody is happy, about complaining over modern wonders like air travel and wifi. The uploader added a note about the comedian's later misconduct.
kBLkX2VaQs4.why: HN commenters bring it up as a reminder to appreciate technology instead of complaining, from Waymo to AI art to flight delays.

kIoZDUd5DKw.summary: Matt Godbolt tells the story of Compiler Explorer, from a hacky basement server to a cloud-scaled service handling tens of thousands of daily requests. He also shows its features and how it is built.
kIoZDUd5DKw.why: Recommended as the source on how Compiler Explorer began and for its lesser-known features like the machine code analyzer.

kLiwvnr4L80.summary: Bill Dally of NVIDIA gives a University of Washington lecture on trends in deep learning hardware. It covers numeric formats, specialized instructions, energy per operation and co-design of hardware and software.
kLiwvnr4L80.why: HN commenters cite it for NVIDIA's perspective on AI hardware efficiency, including logarithmic number formats and energy use.

kTKn1aSOyOs.summary: Tom Lehrer performs his satirical song about rocket scientist Wernher von Braun, with an introduction. It is a two-minute musical clip.
kTKn1aSOyOs.why: HN quotes it in discussions of engineers' moral responsibility and recommends it as a favorite of Lehrer's witty songs.

kTrOg19gzP4.summary: A 2014 talk by Geo Carncross (geocar) demonstrating kOS, a minimalist operating system and programming environment built around the k language, with early screenshots.
kTrOg19gzP4.why: HN commenters recommend it as a rare live look at kOS in action, and one that is fascinating and mind-bending.

k_P7Y0-wgos.summary: A documentary on Clive Wearing, a renowned musician whose brain was damaged by a virus in 1985, leaving him with a memory spanning only about seven seconds. It follows his life and condition.
k_P7Y0-wgos.why: HN points to it as the extended documentary on an extreme case of amnesia whenever memory loss or consciousness comes up.

kc_Jq42Og7Q.summary: A Channel 4 News interview with technologist Jaron Lanier, who argues that social media damages people's lives. He discusses how Facebook, YouTube and Google use algorithms and data collection to shape what users see.
kc_Jq42Og7Q.why: Offered as a concise summary of the economics and manipulation behind social media addiction in Facebook-related threads.

kdsb2wwn-7g.summary: An expat YouTuber in China shows how dockless bike-sharing, once loved, has been flooded by competing companies. Bikes pile up, get abandoned in odd places and are vandalised, with footage from around the city.
kdsb2wwn-7g.why: HN commenters point to it as a brief, accurate insider overview of what went wrong with oversupplied dockless bike sharing.

knbVWXzL4-4.summary: Not Just Bikes explains how Dutch traffic lights use early detection, transit priority and conflict-free design to cut waiting. The aim is to move as many people as possible rather than as many cars.
knbVWXzL4-4.why: Used as the standard reference for what genuinely smart traffic signals look like, in threads about traffic engineering and self-driving cars.

koTf7u0v41o.summary: Emery Berger's CppCon 2020 plenary on why performance is hard on modern hardware after the end of Dennard scaling. It covers benchmarking pitfalls and introduces new profiling tools for finding real bottlenecks.
koTf7u0v41o.why: Recommended for treating benchmarking and profiling scientifically rather than by myth, with innovative tools.

ky1nGQhHTso.summary: Asianometry examines why Japan's software industry has lagged despite its hardware strengths. It looks at dependence on US software and the low prestige of programming.
ky1nGQhHTso.why: Recommended as a good explanation of Japanese software industry struggles, though one commenter is unsure of its accuracy.

kz9wjJjmkmc.summary: A documentary on the 1972 Club of Rome study Limits to Growth, which questioned the pursuit of endless economic growth. It covers the study's findings and whether anyone acted on them.
kz9wjJjmkmc.why: HN commenters point to it as an overview of the Club of Rome's work in threads on systems thinking and collapse.

kN0SVBCJqLs.summary: Steve Jobs introduces the first iPod at a small Apple event in 2001. He positions it as a music player and ties it to the Apple brand.
kN0SVBCJqLs.why: HN commenters use it to compare against later Apple launches, to show how low-key the debut was, and as an example of a great product speech.

kd0xTfdt6qw.summary: Part 2 of Richard Feynman's Messenger Lectures at Cornell, The Character of Physical Law, on the relation of mathematics to physics. He explains why understanding nature requires mathematics.
kd0xTfdt6qw.why: Recommended as a lecture so clear that no formal training is needed to follow it, and cited on why math is needed for physics.

k47u9tduwb8.summary: YouTuber Josh Pieters lists microwave meals on Deliveroo as if from a restaurant and sees whether anyone orders them. The stunt shows how little vetting the platform applied.
k47u9tduwb8.why: HN cites it as an example of delivery platforms accepting listings without hygiene inspection, in ghost kitchen discussions.

kAG39jKi0lI.summary: A BBC comedy sketch from The One Ronnie starring Ronnie Corbett and Harry Enfield, built around a word-play misunderstanding about a broken BlackBerry. It is about three minutes long.
kAG39jKi0lI.why: HN posts it as a joke or light recommendation in threads where dongles, Apple or trademark confusion come up.

kFT54hO1X8M.summary: David Patterson's talk on the history of computer architecture, from RISC and superscalar designs to the end of Dennard scaling and Moore's Law. It argues that domain-specific architectures and open instruction sets open a new golden age.
kFT54hO1X8M.why: Recommended, including by Chris Lattner, as a history of CPU architecture and why performance gains slowed.

kHW-ayt_Urk.summary: James Hamilton of AWS gives a Velocity 2010 keynote on datacenter infrastructure innovation, focused on power and cooling costs and a breakdown of where datacenter spending goes.
kHW-ayt_Urk.why: HN points to it for Hamilton's datacenter cost breakdown and as a primary source for claims about power versus hardware costs.

kJXRyWQgOY4.summary: GreatScott! tests ProLogium lithium ceramic batteries, a solid-state design. He measures their volumetric and gravimetric energy density, compares them to Li-ion and LiPo, and runs durability tests at the end.
kJXRyWQgOY4.why: HN commenters cite it as hands-on testing of a solid-state battery claim, though some remain skeptical until products ship.

kKySEUrP7LA.summary: Paul Biggar's Google Tech Talk on compiling and optimizing scripting languages, drawn from his work on the phc ahead-of-time PHP compiler. He covers runtime typing, aliasing and code generation challenges, and argues AOT can compete with JIT.
kKySEUrP7LA.why: Cited in PHP compiler and language-implementation discussions as an honest account of the real difficulties of compiling dynamic languages.

kRlhlCWplqk.summary: A NASA and Durham University supercomputer simulation suggesting the Moon may have formed within hours of a giant impact between Earth and a Mars-sized body. It is one of the highest-resolution giant-impact simulations run.
kRlhlCWplqk.why: HN commenters link it as a cool visualization whenever Theia and Moon formation come up.

kTXTPe3wahc.summary: Veritasium explains the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics, drawing heavily on Sean Carroll's book. It walks through the Schrodinger equation and why wave collapse may be unnecessary if the universe keeps splitting.
kTXTPe3wahc.why: Recommended as an accessible explanation of many-worlds versus single-world wave collapse.

kWOAHIpmLAI.summary: Aaron Patterson's RailsConf 2011 talk on Rails 3.1 performance, showing why deeper Rack middleware stacks slow Rails and how a shallower pipeline helps. It also touches on Rack API design.
kWOAHIpmLAI.why: Cited in Rails performance and Rack design discussions for Patterson's analysis of stack depth and garbage collection.

kXpzp4RDGJI.summary: A short Harvard Online animation, narrated by Professor Rob Lue, showing how ATP synthase works inside mitochondria. It comes from the HarvardX Cell Biology: Mitochondria course.
kXpzp4RDGJI.why: Linked as a vivid visualization of ATP synthase as a rotary molecular machine, often in discussions of protein machines and cellular energy.

kasiov0ytEc.summary: A TVO current affairs panel debates Canada's Bill C-16, which added gender identity and expression to human rights law and the Criminal Code. Jordan Peterson argues it threatens free speech, and other guests respond.
kasiov0ytEc.why: HN uses it as a source for the compelled-speech argument and the debate around Peterson's position.

kdz6FeQLuHQ.summary: Not Just Bikes looks at traffic in the Bahamas to show that a small country can be just as car-centric as a big one. He ties it to land use, car dependence and how dedicated transit lanes help.
kdz6FeQLuHQ.why: Pointed to as a good rant on car-brained design and as evidence that country size is not what drives car dependence.

kopoLzvh5jY.summary: OpenAI's short demo of agents playing hide-and-seek in a simulated environment. Through self-play, the agents develop six progressively more complex strategies and counter-strategies, including tool use.
kopoLzvh5jY.why: HN uses it as a vivid example of emergent behavior from multi-agent reinforcement learning, and as a way to make AI misalignment concerns feel concrete.

ksb3KD6DfSI.summary: A short compilation showing many local news anchors across different stations reading the same scripted statement verbatim. It is presented as evidence of centralized message control in local media.
ksb3KD6DfSI.why: Used as an example in threads about media consolidation and distrust of news, though many commenters cite it critically or only as a talking point.

kz165f1g8-E.summary: A Veritasium video touring Relativity Space and explaining why 3D printing whole rockets cuts tooling costs, allows rapid iteration, reduces part count and enables new designs. It includes an interview with Scott Manley on aerospace engineering.
kz165f1g8-E.why: Pointed to as a clear explainer of Relativity Space's fully 3D printed rocket approach when rocket manufacturing or additive manufacturing comes up.

k238XpMMn38.summary: A short video that reads out comments from the leaked Team Fortress 2 source code to show the frustration of Valve's programmers over time.
k238XpMMn38.why: HN cites it as an example of messy code behind successful games and of the human stories that code comments can hold.

k4RRi_ntQc8.summary: A one-minute clip from Barack Obama's 2008 Google visit in which Eric Schmidt asks him the most efficient way to sort a million 32-bit integers. Obama answers that bubble sort would be the wrong choice.
k4RRi_ntQc8.why: Used as a joke or aside about bubble sort and as evidence that Obama was tech savvy, not as something recommended for its content.

k5eL_al_m7Q.summary: An art project by Simon Weckert in which 99 smartphones pulled in a handcart create a fake traffic jam on Google Maps. A green street shows as red, which diverts cars to other routes.
k5eL_al_m7Q.why: HN cites it as a playful example of attacking crowd-sourced traffic data and of how automated systems can be fooled.

k5xf40KrK3I.summary: A 54-minute video by a former MrBeast worker alleging that MrBeast's operation is fraudulent, including claims that some contests are staged or manipulated.
k5xf40KrK3I.why: HN mentions it in MrBeast threads as the source of allegations, often in a critical or skeptical context, not as a recommendation.

k7YVxLLIuGM.summary: A deadpan comedy video offering mock advice on defending your car from supermaneuverable fighter jets and air-to-surface missiles. It jokes about installing close-in Gatling guns and radar.
k7YVxLLIuGM.why: Invoked as a joke in threads about large vehicles, car safety and absurd hypothetical scenarios.

k8RRykNVL6E.summary: A teaser for the Skydio 2 Dock, a weatherproof charging base station that enables persistent, automated drone operations for enterprise uses such as site mapping and security patrols.
k8RRykNVL6E.why: Linked from Skydio's job postings in monthly hiring threads to show the product they are building.

kAJaGAMWjHM.summary: A short clip of Romain Dumas and the all-electric VW I.D. R breaking the overall Pikes Peak hillclimb record with a 7:57 run, over 16 seconds faster than the previous best, with footage of the crowd's reaction.
kAJaGAMWjHM.why: Cited as evidence that electric cars can beat combustion cars in racing, here in a hillclimb where altitude and short runs suit electric power.

kAqIJZeeXEc.summary: A one-minute clip from the film Idiocracy featuring the slogan that Brawndo has what plants crave because it has electrolytes.
kAqIJZeeXEc.why: HN uses it only as a joke reference to declining intelligence or silly marketing logic.

kHI7RTKhlz0.summary: A one-minute clip of Steve Ballmer explaining IBM's obsession with counting thousands of lines of code (KLOCs) as a measure of programmers. He explains why that metric is useless.
kHI7RTKhlz0.why: Linked whenever lines of code or developer productivity metrics are debated.

kIc8Rr-cKd8.summary: Real air traffic control audio of the Air Astana flight whose flight controls had been wired in reverse by a maintenance error. The pilots struggle to keep control while ATC tries to help.
kIc8Rr-cKd8.why: Linked as a primary source recording for the reversed-controls incident in aviation safety discussions.

kJ1_P5oqf6Y.summary: A LockPickingLawyer video showing that a padlock sold as an Amazon's Choice high-security product can be opened trivially, with no picking needed.
kJ1_P5oqf6Y.why: HN cites it, along with the rest of the series, as evidence that Amazon's Choice badges do not mean good quality.

kJQP7kiw5Fk.summary: The official music video for Despacito by Luis Fonsi featuring Daddy Yankee, a Latin pop hit that became the most viewed video in YouTube history.
kJQP7kiw5Fk.why: Mentioned as a view-count record holder and as a sample of protected media for downloader and encoder discussions.

kJZ1eHU_JZg.summary: Footage of a crash test of a Boeing 727 deliberately crashed in the Mexican desert, shown from multiple angles inside and outside. It is taken from a Channel 4 documentary.
kJZ1eHU_JZg.why: Cited as an example of airliner crash tests in discussions of crash survivability and seat design.

kMJNEFHj8b8.summary: Microsoft engineers Chiara Mooney and Shiven Mian describe the journey and challenges of building and consuming React Native for Windows inside Microsoft. It was given at Chain React 2023.
kMJNEFHj8b8.why: HN cites it as first-party evidence of where Microsoft uses React Native in Windows, particularly the Start Menu.

kNWfqVWC2KI.summary: A short clip of a jet-powered flying lawnmower, the Sky Cutter, and related RC flying lawnmowers.
kNWfqVWC2KI.why: Cited as a favorite flying oddity and as a joke about projects that get airborne through sheer thrust.

kO5EXjFKE7U.summary: A data-visualization style timeline of the early coronavirus outbreak events by YouTuber Nathan Rich. It lays out dates of key developments in China.
kO5EXjFKE7U.why: Used as a reference timeline in arguments over whether information was suppressed, with commenters noting a possible pro-China bias.

kOO31qFmi9A.summary: A short vintage clip introducing Microsoft Excel in 1990, widely known for its elevator-themed commercial. It shows how spreadsheet software was pitched in that era.
kOO31qFmi9A.why: Cited as a famous 90s Excel ad and as a benchmark for how clear a product ad can be.

kPMHcanq0xM.summary: Magic Leap's original 2015 concept video, made with Weta Workshop, showing what mixed reality could look like. It was posted to explain the company's goals to outsiders.
kPMHcanq0xM.why: Mostly cited as an example of misleading tech marketing, since commenters say it was a rendered concept presented as if it were real product footage.

kQRu7DdTTVA.summary: A short Anthropic ad from its campaign saying ads are coming to AI but not to Claude, using a comedic scenario about getting a six pack quickly.
kQRu7DdTTVA.why: HN cites it as an example of Anthropic mocking OpenAI over ads in ChatGPT, often when ads in chatbots come up.

kSLJriaOumA.summary: A short demo video for NVIDIA's StyleGAN paper, which proposes a style-based generator for GANs. It shows face synthesis with style mixing and scale-specific control over attributes like pose and freckles.
kSLJriaOumA.why: Cited as an example of how realistic GAN-generated faces had become, and of what a well-structured latent space can do.

kUS9uvYyn3A.summary: A short CGP Grey bonus video explaining the shortest-splitline algorithm, which draws electoral districts by repeatedly splitting a state along its shortest dividing line while balancing population. It is offered as a neutral, algorithmic fix for gerrymandering.
kUS9uvYyn3A.why: Cited as the standard example of algorithmic redistricting when gerrymandering and electoral reform come up.

kV2HDM86XgI.summary: A Johns Hopkins Foreign Affairs Symposium debate between former NSA and CIA director Michael Hayden and constitutional law professor David Cole, moderated by Major Garrett. They argue over NSA surveillance, its constitutionality and the balance between privacy and security.
kV2HDM86XgI.why: Used mainly as a source for Hayden's remarks that the 'nothing to hide' argument is a bad one, in privacy threads.

kVY7-Ti77UQ.summary: Musician Benn Jordan explains how all of his music was removed from Spotify and walks through the history of digital music distribution and fake streams. He argues that Spotify's anti-bot measures are mostly a phony war.
kVY7-Ti77UQ.why: HN cites it as a firsthand example of artists losing catalogs with no recourse and of the middlemen in music streaming.

kWSIFh8ICaA.summary: A short, deadpan Sony instructional video from E3 2013 showing how to 'share' a PS4 game by physically handing the disc to a friend. It was Sony's jab at Microsoft's planned restrictions on used games and game sharing for the Xbox One.
kWSIFh8ICaA.why: HN cites it as a famously effective piece of marketing and as Sony's clearest public stance on used games versus Microsoft's.

kaahx4hMxmw.summary: A very short clip from the TV series Westworld about whether it matters if you cannot tell a human from an artificial being.
kaahx4hMxmw.why: HN invokes it as a quick reference in discussions of AI-generated content and indistinguishable AI output.

kdTsbFS4xmI.summary: Tom Scott visits ThyssenKrupp's test tower in Rottweil to see the Multi, a rope-free elevator that uses linear motors to move cabins sideways as well as vertically.
kdTsbFS4xmI.why: HN links it whenever ThyssenKrupp's Multi or paternoster lifts come up, as the clearest look at the working test tower.

kfVsfOSbJY0.summary: The official music video for Rebecca Black's 2011 viral pop song Friday.
kfVsfOSbJY0.why: Brought up as a joke or pop-culture reference, such as bankers being sick of the song.

kikzjTfos0s.summary: David Graeber's RSA lecture on bullshit jobs, expanding on his essay about why so many people do work they believe is pointless. He discusses what this says about the modern economy and the way society values work.
kikzjTfos0s.why: Used as a reference when discussing meaningless work and bureaucracy growth in tech and management.

koqNm_TgOZk.summary: A short Adam Ruins Everything clip arguing that corporations shift blame for litter and waste onto consumers. It touches on the packaging industry's anti-litter campaigns.
koqNm_TgOZk.why: Cited in recycling and plastic-waste threads as an entertaining take on corporate blame-shifting.

ktE_3PrJZO0.summary: A documentary on North Korean defectors in Seoul and the South Korean intelligence service (NIS, formerly KCIA), including accusations of shady dealings.
ktE_3PrJZO0.why: HN cites it for its claims about NIS bribery of defectors and for defectors who say they want to go home.

kw-DlWwlXHo.summary: A Gamereactor interview at E3 2012 with John Carmack, who shows his lag-free head-mounted display running DOOM 3 BFG Edition. He discusses what the headset could mean for the games industry.
kw-DlWwlXHo.why: Cited as an early, primary-source look at Carmack's VR prototype, which preceded his move to Oculus.

kwnWfHq2EfQ.summary: The day 2 keynote at Google Cloud Next '17, announcing new GCP and G Suite products with demos and customer stories from Google leaders.
kwnWfHq2EfQ.why: HN cites it only for specific moments, such as the live Spanner resize demo, the Jamboard demo and the Titan announcement.

kwtt51gvaJQ.summary: A four-minute demo of the greenhouse effect showing how increased carbon dioxide raises temperature. It uses a simple setup that is dramatic and easy to understand.
kwtt51gvaJQ.why: Linked as a simple, replicable demonstration of CO2's greenhouse effect, even in a classroom.

kx1Jxk6kjbQ.summary: Excerpts from Nick Breeze's 2012 interview with researcher Natalia Shakhova about methane release from the East Siberian Arctic Shelf. She discusses the risk of abrupt methane emissions.
kx1Jxk6kjbQ.why: HN cites it in methane and permafrost threads as an early warning that still looks relevant.

kx_G2a2hL6U.summary: A short scene from Monty Python's Life of Brian in which a Roman centurion cannot keep a straight face over the name Biggus Dickus.
kx_G2a2hL6U.why: Used as a joke or allusion in unrelated threads, usually when names or laughter come up, not as something to learn from.
